set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

echo "== verify staged inputs against their pinned sha256 (bwa's inputs, reused verbatim) =="
{ printf '%s  %s\n' 61eba5b05ef7d9ae5310e756c1143fa48072de3856d36871bb14e57aa2435ff3 chr20.fa
  printf '%s  %s\n' 4bd24cdfa4486964f070e69b5dd109b6e1e78561783d48c4e62cc6fae3536a00 HG00096_chr20smoke_1.fq.gz
  printf '%s  %s\n' ebd1ad56bc572a4bf157ba21d1ad8ef074ea25f02eb2d982d9f0089180d82a04 HG00096_chr20smoke_2.fq.gz
} > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

echo "== bowtie2-build (GRCh38 chr20, 64444167 bp) =="
bowtie2-build --threads 4 chr20.fa idx > build.log 2>&1
test -s idx.1.bt2

# --local matches bwa mem's local (soft-clipping) alignment, which is what makes the
# cross-check against bwa valid: bowtie2's DEFAULT is end-to-end (global) alignment,
# which rejects reads bwa soft-clips, so default-vs-bwa disagree by design. See README.
echo "== bowtie2 --local -p 4 (same 400k pairs bwa aligned) =="
bowtie2 --local -p 4 -x idx -1 HG00096_chr20smoke_1.fq.gz -2 HG00096_chr20smoke_2.fq.gz -S out.sam 2> align.log
grep "overall alignment rate" align.log

# Do NOT rm any staged input (chr20.fa / the fastqs / aln.sam): host /tmp is sticky
# (1777) and stage-in writes them as the instance user, so this container (a different
# uid) gets EPERM unlinking them, and `rm -f` does not suppress EPERM. idx*.bt2 and
# out.sam are this task's own files.
echo "== smoke check: conservation + alignment rate + bowtie2<->bwa concordance =="
python3 - > smoke-check.txt <<'PY'
import re,sys
def load(path):
    st={}
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            if line[0]=='@': continue
            p=line.split('\t',6); flag=int(p[1])
            if flag & 0x900: continue                       # primary alignments only
            st[(p[0], 1 if flag & 0x40 else 2)] = 0 if flag & 0x4 else 1   # mapped?
    return st
bt=load('out.sam'); bwa=load('aln.sam')
prim=len(bt); mapped=sum(bt.values())
rate=float(re.search(r'([\d.]+)% overall alignment rate', open('align.log').read()).group(1))
keys=set(bt)&set(bwa); n=len(keys)
conc=sum(1 for k in keys if bt[k]==bwa[k])/n
fail=[]
def chk(label, ok, detail):
    print(f"{label:26s} {detail}")
    if not ok: fail.append(label)
# 400,000 pairs in -> exactly 800,000 primary records out: a conservation identity, no band.
chk("bt2_primary_records", prim==800000, f"{prim}  want exactly 800000 (400k pairs x2, conservation)")
# bowtie2 is deterministic, so these reproduce exactly; bands are for aligner-version drift.
chk("bt2_primary_mapped", 150000<=mapped<=260000, f"{mapped}  want 150000..260000 (observed 206155)")
chk("bt2_alignment_rate_pct", 22.0<=rate<=29.0, f"{rate}  want 22..29 (observed 25.77, --local)")
chk("shared_readmates", n==800000, f"{n}  want 800000 (identical read set to bwa)")
# Cross-code: two independent LOCAL aligners on identical reads+reference agree on which
# reads map. Floor justified by method (residual disagreement is reads at the local-score
# threshold), not picked to pass; deterministic so it cannot go flaky.
chk("concordance_vs_bwa", conc>=0.90, f"{conc:.4f}  want >=0.90 (observed 0.9462)")
if fail: print("FAILED: "+", ".join(fail)); sys.exit(1)
PY
cat smoke-check.txt
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
